name: Chung Shu
bio: Chung Shu (仲殊; Zhongshu; 11th–12th century) was a writer of ci, the Chinese song lyrics composed to set tunes, in the Song dynasty. He was a Buddhist monk.
The single ci here is from the chinese-poetry dataset of Zhu Zumou's 1924 anthology Three Hundred Song Lyrics (宋词三百首), in simplified characters, with the tune name as title.

poems.title: 夏云峰 (Xia yun feng)
poems.author: Chung Shu
poems.collection: 宋詞三百首 (Three Hundred Song Lyrics)
poems.text:
天阔云高，溪横水远。
晚日寒生轻晕。
闲阶静、杨花渐少，朱门掩、莺声犹嫩。
悔匆匆、过却清明，旋占得馀芳，已成幽恨。
都几日阴沈，连宵慵困。
起来韶华都尽。
怨入双眉闲斗损。
乍品得情怀，看承全近。
深深态、无非自许。
厌厌意、终羞人间。
争知道、梦里蓬莱，待忘了馀香，时传音信。
纵留得莺花，东风不住，也则眼前愁闷。
